alt: Three overlapping ellipses labelled Consistency, Availability and Partition Tolerance. The overlaps are labelled CA, CP and AP, and no region is shared by all three.
author: JamieMcCarthy

alt: A coordinator box at the top is joined to three nodes. Each node has its own memory holding data and processes, and its own disk with tables, logs and control files.
author: Scifipete

alt: Server A writes data to a primary database (step 1). The primary copies the data to a target database, which acknowledges it (step 2). Server B then reads from the target (step 3).
author: Michel Bakni

alt: A two-column table. Keys K1 to K5 on the left, each paired with a value on the right such as AAA,BBB,CCC.
author: Clescop

alt: Two documents with named fields (title, teachers, classes taught) pointed to by two keys, IIR and OPL. The first document has an extra field that the second does not.
author: JuliaL0313

alt: A property graph. Nodes Alice and Bob (people with name and age) and a node Chess (a group) are joined by labelled arrows such as knows and is_member, each with an id and a since date.
author: Ole Mussmann

alt: Twelve numbered people in a population. Four of them, numbers 2, 5, 8 and 10, are picked at random and moved to a sample.
author: Dan Kernler

alt: Twelve numbered people in a row. Every third person, numbers 2, 5, 8 and 11, is moved into the sample.
author: Dan Kernler

alt: A data source or message queue feeds two paths. A speed (real-time) processing path and a batch processing path each have their own store, and queries are answered from both.
author: Textractor

alt: A row of 18 bits. Three items x, y and z each set three bits to 1 through three hash functions. A fourth item w points to three bits, one of which is 0, so w is definitely not in the set.
author: David Eppstein

alt: Three small boards show the step cost from the centre square for Chebyshev (a king, all eight neighbours cost 1), Euclidean (diagonals cost root 2) and Taxicab (diagonals cost 2). A larger board shows the same two squares are 4 apart for the king, 5 for the ant and 7 for the rook.
author: Cmglee

alt: A city street grid. Red, blue and yellow routes of right-angle steps join two points and are all equally long. A green straight diagonal line between the same points is shorter.
author: Psychonaut

alt: Two points p and q on x and y axes. The straight line between them is the longest side of a right triangle whose other sides are q1 minus p1 and q2 minus p2, so d squared equals the sum of the two squared differences.
author: Kmhkmh

alt: Two overlapping circles A and B. The overlap, labelled A intersection B, is shaded.
author: Stephan Kulla

alt: Two overlapping circles A and B. Both circles together, labelled A union B, are shaded.
author: Stephan Kulla

alt: Two arrows x and y from one point with the angle theta between them marked, and the formula theta equals arccos of x dot y divided by the lengths of x and y.
author: BenFrantzDale

alt: A cube whose eight corners are the 3-bit strings 000 to 111 and whose edges each flip one bit. A red path from 100 to 011 has three edges and a blue path from 010 to 111 has two.
author: Cburnett

alt: Three triangles with sides x and y and a base z. In each one z is shorter than x plus y, and as the triangle gets flatter z gets closer to x plus y.
author: WhiteTimberwolf, Brews ohare (PNG version)

alt: Two columns of bits. On the left a stored string is cut into four pieces and each piece sets one bit to 1. On the right a query string is cut into two pieces: the first points to a bit that is 1 and the second, drawn in red, points to a bit that is 0.
author: Emreerhan

alt: Five curves of e to the power minus x divided by or times a constant, all starting at 1 and falling towards 0. A small decay constant gives a very slow fall and a large one gives a very fast fall.
author:

derivative work: Autopilot (talk)
